gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'max' wattage printed for single-DIN CD receivers is a peak figure: the Sony MEX-N5300BT's 55 W x 4 max, which looks the highest, comes with the lowest continuous rating (20 W x 4 RMS). The Pioneer DEH-S4220BT and Kenwood KDC-BT282U are both rated 50 W x 4 max and 22 W x 4 RMS.
standout_why: I opened itechguides.com (How to Play CDs in a Modern Car, 2026-10-11) and ensightauto.com (How to Add a CD Player to a Car, 2026-02-04). Neither gives any wattage, peak or continuous. They list battery hours, anti-skip seconds and USB-port conditions for cheap portables only. ChatGPT's own answer showed the Pioneer DEH-S31BT with no power figure. Our current page lists only the max figures (50/55/50 W x 4), so a reader would think the Sony is the strongest.
decides: This confirms the in-dash picks rather than flipping them. On continuous power the three decks are within 2 W of each other (20 to 22 W x 4 RMS), so the higher Sony max figure is not a reason to choose it. Power should not decide between them. What separates them is preouts: Pioneer has 2 pairs at 4 V, Sony has 3 pairs at 4 V and Kenwood has 1 pair at 2.5 V. That matters only if the shopper plans to add an amplifier. The table's power column should show RMS first, with max in a footnote.
